# Collecting Keywords {#sec-keywords}

A search engine matches words. If the authors of a paper used a different word from yours, the search misses the paper. This chapter shows how we collected the words that authors in this field use.

## Each field has its own name for the idea

The same idea appears under different names in different fields. These are the names we found in titles and abstracts during our search:

| Name used by authors | Where we found it |
| --- | --- |
| double-entry bookkeeping | title of @ellerman2014 |
| group of differences, Pacioli group | abstract of @ellerman2014 |
| double entry multidimensional accounting | title of @ellerman1986 |
| algebraic model of accounting systems | title of @nehmer1997 |
| algebraic automaton | title of @rambaud2005 |
| matrix-based accounting system | title of @leech1986 |
| inferring transactions from financial statements | title of @arya2000 |
| bookkeeping graphs | title of @liang2023 |
| partita doppia, spans of reflexive graphs | title and abstract of @katis2008 |
| triple-entry bookkeeping | title of @ijiri1986 |
| 簿記代数 (Japanese: "bookkeeping algebra") | title of @ozawa2023matrix |

Two lessons follow from this table.

First, the name of a mathematical structure can be a sharper search term than the name of the subject. The abstract of @ellerman2014 introduces the name "Pacioli group" for the group of differences used in bookkeeping, so the term points to this line of work.

Second, the historical Italian name *partita doppia* is the title of a category theory paper [@katis2008]. Its title does not contain the English words "double-entry bookkeeping," so a search restricted to titles in English would miss it. In our search it appeared in response to a Google Scholar query that combined "double-entry," "bookkeeping," and "category theory."

## Where the words came from

We collected these terms in a loop:

1. Search with the words we already had.
2. Read the titles and abstracts of the results.
3. Add any new names for the idea to the list.
4. Search again with the new words.

The loop stops when new searches return only papers already in the log. In our search, the first query used the words "algebra," "bookkeeping," and "double-entry." The term "Pacioli group" came from the abstract of the first relevant paper, and "bookkeeping graphs" came from a later query that added "graph theory."

## Keywords in a second language

For Japanese sources we used terms taken from Japanese titles. The term 簿記代数 ("bookkeeping algebra") appears in a Japanese paper title [@ozawa2023matrix], and searching for that exact term in a Japanese database found that paper directly (@sec-japanese).

## Exercises

1. For your topic from @sec-question, list at least five names for the central idea. For each, record where you found it.
2. Run the loop in this chapter twice. Record in your log which new terms the second round added.
3. Find one term for your topic in a language other than English. Search for it, and compare the results with the English search.
